chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Mutamatti' who finds the price but does not find the sheep, he said: He should leave the price with one of the people of Mecca, and instruct someone to buy for him and slaughter on his behalf, and that would suffice for him. So if Dhu al-Hijjah passes, he delays that to the Dhu al-Hijjah of the next year.

key_terms.مُتَمِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in the same season

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who has money for the sacrifice but no animal?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the practical flexibility within Hajj al-Tamattu', allowing a pilgrim to delegate the procurement and slaughter of the Hadi (sacrificial animal) to a trusted agent in Mecca. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the obligation is fulfilled through the act of slaughter, even if the physical animal is acquired by another, and permits deferring the sacrifice to the next year if the animal is not found, ensuring the ritual remains valid without undue hardship.
